T: Seconds for everybody. Thirds for Sherman.
D: A kind, heavy-set professor tests his own weight-loss formula and turns into Buddy Love, a slick, cocky alter ego who will not go away.
P: Pass the fried chicken when talk at the Klump table turns to the calories in the skin.
S: Hartley's ten million dollar crab cakes
Golden crab cakes with lemon mayo, for Hartley's ten million dollar cheque.

Mix the crab, breadcrumbs, 3 tbsp mayo, egg, spring onion and seasoning gently, and shape into 8 cakes. Coat in the panko and chill for 15 minutes so they hold. Stir the 125g mayo with the capers, mustard, hot sauce and a squeeze of lemon for the remoulade. Shallow fry the cakes until deep golden on both sides, about 3 minutes a side. Drain and serve with the remoulade and lemon wedges.
60g fresh breadcrumbs, plus 60g panko for coating@Pantry
3 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise, plus 125g for the remoulade@Pantry
1 tsp Old Bay or Cajun seasoning@Spices
Ernie Junior laughs his dinner out.

Heat a 25cm cast-iron pan in the oven at 200C. Whisk the dry ingredients, then stir in the eggs, buttermilk and melted butter until just combined. Pour into the hot greased pan and bake until golden and springy. Whip the softened butter with the honey and a pinch of salt and serve with the cornbread in wedges.
M: Buttermilk chicken fried crackling, mashed potatoes and gravy. The skin holds all the calories.

Soak the chicken in the buttermilk and hot sauce for at least 2 hours, or overnight. Mix the flour with the paprika, garlic powder, cayenne and 2 tsp salt, and dredge the chicken twice, pressing it on. Fry in 170C oil in batches, turning, until deep golden and cooked through, about 14 minutes. Drain on a rack. Boil the potatoes until soft, then mash with 60g butter and the hot milk. Cook the remaining butter and 2 tbsp flour, whisk in the stock and simmer to a peppery gravy.
1.2kg chicken thighs and drumsticks, skin on@Meat
250g plain flour, plus 2 tbsp for the gravy@Pantry
Buddy Love's T-bone with baked potato
A big T-bone grilled to medium rare, crisp baked potato. Buddy orders six at The Scream.

Rub the potatoes with oil and salt and bake at 200C until crisp outside and soft inside. Bring the steaks to room temperature, season well and grill on a very hot barbecue or pan to medium-rare, about 5 minutes a side. Rest the steaks while you wilt the spinach with the butter and garlic, then simmer with the cream and parmesan until thick. Split the potatoes and fill with sour cream and chives, and serve with the steak and spinach.
W: Chocolate ice cream with marshmallows and nuts, hot fudge poured over. Buddy's Rocky Road punchline gets Reggie.

Soften the ice cream for 10 minutes, fold in half the marshmallows and half the peanuts and refreeze. Heat the cream with the golden syrup until steaming and stir in the chocolate until glossy. Scoop the ice cream into glasses, pour over the hot fudge and finish with the rest of the marshmallows, peanuts and a cherry.
K: Fresh lemonade with raspberry syrup floated on top, turning pink as you stir.

Stir the lemon juice and sugar with 250ml cold water until the sugar dissolves. Fill 4 glasses with ice, pour in the lemonade and top with soda water. Spoon 1 tbsp raspberry syrup over the back of a spoon into each so it sinks, and stir at the table.
